title: The Best Facebook Ad Library Alternatives in 2026 (Free & Paid)
summary: Compare the best Facebook Ad Library alternatives for competitor research, ad history, creative analysis and API access. Includes free and paid tools for 2026.
body_markdown:
Meta’s **Facebook Ad Library** (now the Meta Ads Library) is the most complete record of ads on Facebook and Instagram. It is free, it needs no login, and in 2026 it finally shows an impression range for every ad. It is still the wrong tool for a marketer who wants to *do* something with what they find: it cannot compare brands, it keeps no history for ordinary commercial ads, it exports nothing, and it tells you nothing about which ads are working.


This guide ranks the best Facebook Ad Library alternatives in 2026, free and paid, and closes with dedicated sections for the tools people most often want to replace: AdSpy, AdEspresso, BigSpy, Minea and Foreplay.

## Why look for a Facebook Ad Library alternative in 2026


The library improved this year. Every ad now carries an impression-range bucket you can sort by, Threads and WhatsApp are separate placement filters, and ads shown in the EU expose reach by age and gender, the targeting the advertiser chose, and who paid. Used well (see[how to see competitors’ Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-see-competitors-facebook-ads) ), it answers “what is this brand running right now?” for free.


It still fails at the questions that matter for planning:


- **No comparison.** One Page at a time. There is no way to line up five competitors and see who launches more, runs video, or leans on discounts.
- **No history for commercial ads.** Once an ordinary ad stops, it disappears outside the EU. Political ads are archived for seven years; your competitor’s Black Friday creative is not.
- **No analysis.** Hooks, offers, formats and CTAs are yours to tally by hand.
- **No export.** No download, no board, no CSV.
- **No performance signal beyond run length and the coarse impression bucket.** Spend, clicks and conversions are never published.
- **Slow.** Infinite scroll, no bulk view, frequent rate limits.


Every alternative below fixes some of these. The right pick depends on whether you want analysed ads (a library), a searchable archive (a spy tool), or a place to keep what you find (a swipe file).


## The best Facebook Ad Library alternatives


### 1. Sprites Ads Library (free, no login, AI analysis)


The[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) indexes the live ads of dozens of fast-growing tech and SaaS companies (Cursor, Lovable, ElevenLabs and more) across Meta, Google and LinkedIn, read directly from the public libraries and refreshed weekly. Where the Meta Ads Library gives you a wall of creatives, each Sprites advertiser page gives you the analysis: hooks, CTAs, format mix, landing-page destinations, run length, launch tempo and an estimated spend range, calculated using Sprites’ proprietary AI model from the public data.


- No account needed to browse. Full advertiser pages open with an email.
- One page per company, so comparison is a matter of opening two tabs.
- Curated galleries of[Facebook ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/facebook-ad-examples) ,[Google ads examples](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/google-ads-examples) ,[LinkedIn ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/linkedin-ad-examples) and[SaaS ads](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/saas-ad-examples) .
- For a brand that is not in the index, the Sprites copilot pulls its live Meta, Google and LinkedIn ads on request and turns them into a competitor analysis you can act on.


The Sprites Ads Library: search a company, read its ads across Meta, Google and LinkedIn. A company page: Cursor’s live Facebook and Instagram ads, each with its run length. The same page carries Google and LinkedIn.


Limits: the index is focused on technology and SaaS advertisers. If you sell candles on Shopify, a dropshipping spy tool below will have more of your direct competitors.


### 2. The Meta Ads Library, used properly (free)


Before paying for anything, learn the three features most people miss. Wrap a phrase in quotes to search exact copy, separate words with a vertical bar to match any of them, and switch the country to an EU member state to unlock the transparency tab with reach, age and gender breakdowns and the advertiser’s targeting choices. Sort by the impression bucket to skip the ads nobody saw. It remains a single-brand tool, but it is the source every other tool reads from.


### 3. BigSpy (free plan; $9 Basic, $99 Pro)


The largest database at the lowest entry price, across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Pinterest, with engagement and run-time filters. Dated interface, shallow free tier. The default paid pick for a solo advertiser.


### 4. AdSpy ($149/month, flat)


The deepest Facebook and Instagram archive and the only tool that searches ad comments. Agencies live in it; a single brand rarely needs it. See theAdSpy alternatives section below for cheaper routes.


### 5. Minea (free lite; $49 to $399/month)


Built for ecommerce and dropshipping: ad search across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Pinterest paired with product, shop and influencer analysis. Credits meter usage. The pick when the question is “which products are selling?”


### 6. Foreplay ($59 to $459/month)


The best swipe file in the category: a Chrome extension that saves any ad into tagged boards, competitor tracking on higher tiers, and briefs generated from saved ads. Expensive if all you want is a lookup.


### 7. PowerAdSpy (from about $69/month)


Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Google, native and Reddit in one search. Thinner on Meta than AdSpy, but the only tool here that covers YouTube and native without a second subscription.


### 8. Pipiads (from $49/month)


The largest TikTok ad archive, with Facebook as a secondary database and product research features that overlap with Minea. Credit-metered, with a 500-credit free trial.


### 9. Dropispy (free; $29.90/month Premium)


The budget dropshipping option: Facebook-focused, a free tier, and Premium at $29.90 a month ($14.90 on annual billing). Smaller archive, simpler filters, lowest-risk subscription for a first store.


### 10. Turbo Ad Finder 2.0 (free Chrome extension)


Filters your own Facebook feed so it shows only ads. Free and still maintained in 2026 (version 2.0 is the live listing), useless for brand-level research because you only see what Meta shows *you* . Inspiration, not competitor work.

### Beyond Facebook: the other free ad libraries


Meta is not the only platform with a public library. The[Google Ads Transparency Center](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-ads-transparency-center) shows every verified advertiser’s Search, YouTube, Display and Gmail ads for a year after they last ran. The LinkedIn Ad Library is searchable by company or keyword with impression brackets per ad. TikTok’s Creative Center shows top ads by industry and region, and its Commercial Content Library covers EU transparency. The[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) reads all three of the Meta, Google and LinkedIn sources into one page per advertiser.

## AdSpy alternatives


AdSpy’s $149 flat fee buys the deepest Meta archive and comment search. If that is more than you need, three tools cover most of the same ground: **BigSpy** ($99 Pro, free plan) has a comparable database across more platforms with weaker comment search; **PowerAdSpy** adds YouTube, Google and native for a similar total; **Minea** is the better choice if the real question is which products are selling. For a free starting point, the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) gives analysed competitor ads without a database subscription. Our full ranking is in[the best Facebook ad spy tools in 2026](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/facebook-ad-spy-tool) .


## AdEspresso alternatives


AdEspresso by Hootsuite is still available, but it is a Facebook and Instagram campaign manager with A/B testing, not a research tool, and its development has slowed since the acquisition. People searching for an AdEspresso alternative usually want one of two things. For **competitor research** , any library or spy tool on this page replaces the ad-examples feature it never really had. For **campaign management** , an AI agent such as[Sprites for Meta Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-ads-ai) handles creation, testing, budget changes and reporting from a chat, with your approval on every change, and works across Google and LinkedIn as well.


## BigSpy alternatives


BigSpy wins on price and platform breadth and loses on interface, data freshness on smaller pages, and the shallow free tier. **AdSpy** is the upgrade for Meta depth and comment search. **Minea** is the upgrade for ecommerce product research. **Dropispy** is the cheaper sideways move. The **Sprites Ads Library** is the free alternative when you want the analysis done for you rather than a bigger haystack.


## Minea alternatives


Minea’s credit metering frustrates heavy users, and its strength is products rather than brands. **Pipiads** is the closest alternative for TikTok-led stores; **BigSpy** and **Dropispy** are cheaper for Facebook-only research; **AdSpy** is the choice when you need archive depth rather than product feeds. For a free brand-level view with hooks and CTAs already tagged, use the[Sprites Ads Library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) .


## Foreplay alternatives


Foreplay is the best swipe file on the market, and that is also its limit: it saves and organises ads far better than it finds them, and $59 a month is a lot for a bookmarking tool. If you mainly need to **discover** competitor ads, the Sprites Ads Library (free) or BigSpy (from $9) do that job. If you need **creative analytics on your own account** as well as competitor swipes, Atria (from $129 a month, annual) and Motion (repriced upward in 2026) compete with Foreplay’s Lens tier. MagicBrief, once the obvious alternative, closed on 31 July 2026 after its acquisition by Canva.


## What to use each alternative for


- **Weekly competitor check:** Sprites Ads Library advertiser pages, or the Meta Ads Library sorted by impressions.
- **Finding a winning product:** Minea, Pipiads or Dropispy.
- **Copywriting research:** AdSpy comment search, or a keyword search in the Meta Ads Library with quoted phrases.
- **Creative briefs and swipe files:** Foreplay.
- **Cross-platform view of one competitor:** Sprites Ads Library (Meta, Google, LinkedIn on one page) or PowerAdSpy.
- **Turning research into live campaigns:** Sprites, where the same copilot that pulled the competitor’s ads can draft, launch and report on yours.


An alternative library only pays off if the ads inside it become decisions.[Creative analytics](https://www.sprites.ai/creative-analytics) is the step that does that, and[what is creative analytics](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/what-is-creative-analytics) covers the metrics and the weekly workflow behind it.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is the Facebook Ad Library free?


Yes. The Meta Ad Library at facebook.com/ads/library is free and needs no account. It shows every active ad from any Page, and for ads shown in the EU it also shows reach, targeting and who paid. What it lacks is speed and analysis: no cross-brand comparison, no export, no history for ordinary commercial ads, and no view of what is working.


### Can you download ads from the Facebook Ad Library?


Not directly. The library has no export or bulk download, which is the main reason marketers look for an alternative. Paid spy tools such as BigSpy and AdSpy add downloads and saved boards. The Sprites Ads Library keeps each creative, its copy, CTA and landing page on the advertiser page, and the Sprites copilot can pull a brand’s live ads into a document you keep.


### How do I find competitor ads without the Facebook Ad Library?


Three routes work. A free ad library such as Sprites indexes dozens of fast-growing advertisers with hooks, CTAs and run length already analysed. Paid ad spy tools such as BigSpy, AdSpy or Minea search hundreds of millions of ads by keyword with engagement filters. For Google and LinkedIn, the Google Ads Transparency Center and the LinkedIn Ad Library are free and searchable by advertiser.


### What is the best free alternative to the Facebook Ad Library?


The Sprites Ads Library is the strongest free option for research: no account, ads from dozens of fast-growing companies across Meta, Google and LinkedIn, with hooks, CTAs, formats and run length already analysed. BigSpy’s free plan (five queries a day) and Dropispy’s free tier are the best free entry points to a large searchable database.


### Are paid Facebook ad spy tools worth it in 2026?


For agencies, dropshippers and multi-product advertisers, usually yes. BigSpy Pro ($99/month), AdSpy ($149/month) and Minea ($49 to $399/month) add search across hundreds of millions of ads, engagement filters and ad history that the library never shows. A single-brand team researching a handful of competitors gets most of the value from the free options.


### What is the best AdSpy alternative?


BigSpy is the closest like-for-like alternative at a lower price ($99/month for Pro, with a free plan). Minea suits ecommerce and dropshipping research, Foreplay suits creative teams building swipe files, and the Sprites Ads Library is the free option when you want analysed competitor ads rather than a raw database.


### What replaced AdEspresso for ad research?


AdEspresso is still sold by Hootsuite, but it is a campaign management and A/B testing tool for Facebook and Instagram, and its ad research features have not kept pace. For competitor research most teams pair a free ad library such as Sprites with a spy tool such as BigSpy; for campaign management, an AI agent such as Sprites for Meta Ads covers creation, testing and reporting.
